name: Treaty with the Delawares, 1866
nations: Lenape (Delaware) of Kansas; now the Delaware Tribe of Indians
promises: Article 1: the United States to secure and pay the Delawares the full value of the land and improvements sold to the Leavenworth, Pawnee and Western Railroad under the 1860 and 1861 treaties.
Article 2: the rest of the Kansas reservation to be sold to the Missouri River Railroad Company or others in a body at not less than $2.50 an acre plus improvements.
Article 4: the United States to sell the Delawares a tract in the Indian Territory, 160 acres for each person who moved, at the price the United States paid.
Article 5: the United States guaranteed peaceable possession of the new home and protection from hostile Indians and civil strife.
today: Royce (p. 841) records that by an agreement with the Cherokee approved April 11, 1867 the Delawares merged their tribal existence with the Cherokee and took up residence in the Cherokee country. No court, claims-commission or government finding of a breach of this treaty was found. In Delaware Tribe of Indians v. United States, 74 Ct. Cl. 368 (1932), the Court of Claims dismissed the tribe's claims for the gold premium on funds, including school-fund distributions made in 1872-1875 under this treaty to Delawares who took citizenship, and on the $286,742.15 railroad payment that Article 1 guaranteed. The Indian Claims Commission Delaware awards located concern other treaties.

openQuestions: Whether the Delawares received a separate tract under Article 4, and whether Article 1 payments were made, was not settled; the 1867 Cherokee agreement replaced the separate home.
The Delaware Tribe of Indians' pages on the Kansas removal returned errors and could not be read; secondary summaries say the tribe could not secure the reservation it expected.
Delaware Indians v. Cherokee Nation, 193 U.S. 127 (1904) concerns the 1867 agreement and is a lead.
treaties.json gives the Delaware Nation, Oklahoma as present-day tribe; the Kansas Delawares who moved in 1867 are the Delaware Tribe of Indians. Not edited.

Audit 2026-11-08: 74 Ct. Cl. 368 (1932, dismissed) added to today. Lead: the Court of Claims in United States v. Delaware Tribe of Indians, 192 Ct. Cl. 385 (1970), records that twelve Delaware suits were settled for $150,000 under the Act of April 21, 1904 (33 Stat. 222); which claims those suits covered, and whether any arose under this treaty, was not traced. A settlement would be litigation, not a finding.
